# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Secuura SEAT A: TWO PRs in ONE pass — #868 (KS-914, tier 1) NO-GO and #867 (KS-913, tier 2) PASS** (2026-09-06 20:44→21:03 AEST, ~19 min for both; batched into one tester session on Kam's credit instruction, two separate verdicts delivered as commissioned) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **The strongest pass this fleet has produced.** Two Majors on A, neither about the security property: **A-1** the 10 s deadline became a socket-IDLE timer, driven on the REAL exported functions at both SHAs against TEST-NET-2 — declared 3000 ms, **elapsed 75014 ms** (base 10005 ms), plus a drip-feed manifestation, with the honest qualifier that for one of the two call sites it is not a regression because the base passed no signal at all. **A-2** the red-proof binds the helper, not the shipped path: stripping `lookup:` from the two agents inside `safeOutboundRequest` left **778 passed, 0 failed**. It also UPHELD what held, measured rather than accepted: the 59 inherited cells proven untouched BY SET (`comm -23` empty) and proven still to BIND the refactored resolver; TLS identity driven through the real function with a wrong-SAN certificate correctly refused and the server's SNI callback seeing the hostname; **a PUBLIC RETRACTION of its own IPv6 result** after finding the fault was in its own loopback instrument, not the product; and it BUILT the merged tree as a real commit and ran the suite (781/781) because a clean textual merge is not a clean behavioural one. On B it classified all 20 remaining files, hashed the SQL gate byte-identical at both SHAs, and found the comment's ORG_ADMIN count wrong (three claimed, four real — Wednesday re-counted it independently with a control). |
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s140, seat A) | **KS-914 round 1 (PR #868)** — `b77b20bf6` → `6f0e145e4` (the core-only pinned `lookup`: resolve once, classify, hand the agent a lookup that returns the validated address; 5 files +309/−46; 65/65 cells; the 59 inherited cells deliberately untouched) | 1 | **0.70** | 0.70 | **NO GO at the gate, fix round 1 of 2.** The security property IS delivered and was measured four ways — this is not a failed fix. Two Majors ride alongside it: a 10 s deadline silently became a socket-idle timer (75 s measured against an unroutable destination, unbounded under a drip-feed, and the body drained for a body no caller reads), and the red-proof binds `pinnedLookup` rather than `safeOutboundRequest`, so removing the pinning from the only shipped path leaves the suite green. Two Minors of honesty: comments claiming blocked and failed "stay distinguishable at the call site" when the return type has one arm and no discriminator, and the redirect change undocumented in both the PR body and the header. Credit where it is due: it stated what it had NOT proven in three places, refused to weaken the guard to test the guard, and its own `~5004 ms` figure turned out to be vitest's `testTimeout` rather than a connect timeout — which the gate caught and it had no way to see. |
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s140, seat A) | **KS-913 round 1 (PR #867)** — `4291a31f` → `1a661bcb9` (one seed row's real identity replaced with `org.admin@example.com` / `Demo Org Admin`; the doc-comment above it rewritten) | 1 | **0.90** | 0.90 | **PASS.** Every DoD line measured and met: the SQL gate byte-identical (sha256 at both SHAs), the row id appearing in exactly one place in the tree, the seed-gate suite 24/24 at both SHAs, `example.com` confirmed NULL-MX. Deductions, both Minor and both in the paragraph the PR itself rewrote: the ORG_ADMIN count

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.

> ## ✅ DONE 2026-08-20 ~08:1x — Kam SENT the re-issue same hour ("email sent").
> Landed i
